title: BHP and Vale face $44 billion civil claim in Brazil over dam disaster
主要内容: BHP and Vale are facing a $44 billion civil claim in Brazil over the dam disaster at their joint venture Samarco. The incident occurred on November 5, 2015, when two dams at the mine in Mariana, Minas Gerais, collapsed, releasing tons of waste and causing extensive damage. Federal prosecutors in Minas Gerais and neighboring Espírito Santo state have demanded R$155 billion ($44 billion) in damages, citing the clean-up costs of the BP oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico. The claim is based on the premise that the human, economic, and socio-environmental impacts of the dam collapse are at least equivalent to those of the BP spill. The suit comes after Vale and BHP settled a R$20 billion lawsuit with the federal and state governments in March. However, independent prosecutors criticized the government for 'selling out' and vowed to seek more compensation. Vale's shares fell over 6% in São Paulo, and BHP's shares dropped by more than 5%. The prosecutors also demanded that Vale, BHP, and Samarco deposit R$7.7 billion into an independently managed fund within 30 days. A judge must decide whether to proceed with the case. The case highlights the ongoing legal and financial challenges faced by the companies following the environmental disaster. BHP and Vale are facing a $44 billion civil claim in Brazil over a dam disaster. The claim is related to the failure of a mining dam, which resulted in significant environmental and human damage. The Brazilian government has been involved in the case, and in February, federal prosecutor José Adércio Leite Sampaio, who has led investigations into the dam failure, told the Financial Times that he planned further lawsuits against the miners, using the BP Deepwater Horizon oil spill as a parameter. This indicates that the legal actions are being taken seriously, with comparisons to other major environmental disasters. The case highlights the ongoing issues in the mining industry regarding safety and environmental responsibility.
